title: What Is llms.txt and Should You Add One?
excerpt: What llms.txt is, who reads it, what two large studies show, whether to add one, how to write one with a sample file, how to test it and what to do first instead.

meta._yoast_wpseo_title: What Is llms.txt? Should You Add One? | Reinforce Lab
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: What is llms.txt, who reads it, and should you add one? What Google says and what two studies of 137,000 and 300,000 sites found, plus how to write one.
meta.rl_answer: llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file at the root of a website that gives language models a short guide to the site and links to its best pages. It is not a standard. Google says Search does not use it, Ahrefs found 97% of llms.txt files got no requests in a month, and SE Ranking found no link to citations. It is cheap to add, but do access, readable pages and clear answers first.
meta.rl_faqs:
What is llms.txt? | llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file, written in Markdown and placed at /llms.txt, that gives language models a short summary of a site and links to its most useful pages. Jeremy Howard proposed it in September 2024. It is not an official web standard.
Is llms.txt a standard? | No. It is a proposal published at llmstxt.org. No major AI platform has committed to reading it, and Google says Google Search does not use it.
Does llms.txt work? | We found no evidence that it improves citations. SE Ranking's analysis of nearly 300,000 domains found no link, and Ahrefs found that 97% of llms.txt files in a 137,210-domain sample received no requests in May 2026. Both have limits, so test it yourself.
Do ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini read llms.txt? | Evidence is thin. Ahrefs saw some requests from GPTBot and Claude Code, but a fetch is not a read, and AI bots did not look for missing files. Google says Search ignores it. OpenAI's documentation focuses on OAI-SearchBot access.
How do I create an llms.txt file? | Pick 10 to 30 useful pages, write a one or two sentence summary, list links under clear headings with short notes, keep it accurate, publish it at yoursite.com/llms.txt and update it when facts change. A generator can draft it, but read the output.
Where do I put llms.txt? | At the root of your site, for example yoursite.com/llms.txt, or at a subpath such as /docs/llms.txt to cover only that section. It should return a normal 200 response and show as plain text.
Does llms.txt replace robots.txt? | No. llms.txt guides content discovery, but it does not allow or block crawlers. Use robots.txt and your firewall settings for access.
Will llms.txt hurt my SEO? | Google says that having an llms.txt file will neither help nor harm your visibility in Google Search. The main risk is a stale file that lists wrong prices or removed pages.
Should I use an llms.txt generator? | You can, since the file is short and tools can draft it from your sitemap. Read the result and remove thin, old or private pages. Writing it by hand takes little time and lets you choose the pages that matter.
Who should add llms.txt? | Documentation and API sites are the best candidates, since coding tools may read it. For most marketing sites it is optional. Fix crawler access, readable HTML, answer-first pages, consistent facts and mentions first.

meta.rl_takeaways:
llms.txt is a proposal by Jeremy Howard from September 2024: a Markdown file at /llms.txt with a summary and links. It is not a web standard.
Google says Google Search does not use llms.txt, and that having one will neither help nor harm your Google visibility.
Ahrefs studied 137,210 domains in May 2026: 28% had a file and 97% of those received no requests. Fetches are not reads.
SE Ranking studied nearly 300,000 domains: 10.13% had a file and it found no link to AI citations. It is observational data.
The file may suit documentation sites, where coding tools could read it. That is an inference to test.
It does not allow or block crawlers. Use robots.txt for that.
Do access, HTML content, answer-first pages, consistent facts and honest mentions before llms.txt.
meta.rl_g_glossary:
llms.txt | A proposed Markdown file that gives language models a short guide to a site and links to its best pages.
Markdown | A simple text format that uses symbols such as # and - for headings and lists.
Crawler | A program that fetches web pages for a search index or an AI tool.
robots.txt | A file that tells crawlers which parts of a site they may fetch.
Agent | An AI tool that takes actions or reads pages on a user's behalf.
Citation | A link to your page shown as a source in an AI answer.
